title: Eviction priority inversion causing tenant isolation regressions — throttles, smoothing, and recovery action items
creator: Marco Nguyen
description: Summary: During a high-concurrency capacity spike on 2026-02-14 we observed a cascade of cache misses and latency spikes originating from an eviction priority inversion in the KV prefix cache. The inversion caused active hot entries for multiple high-throughput tenants to be evicted in favor of lower-utility objects, which amplified cold token generation, increased GPU inference load, and triggered autoscaling thrash. Separately, manual remediation highlighted a slow-release path in slab reference counts that surfaced as a transient memory retention (leak) when preemption and concurrent compaction overlapped. This ticket consolidates investigation notes, mitigations applied, and concrete action items to prevent recurrence.
timeline: 2026-02-14T03:12Z - PagerDuty alert: fleet-wide latency 99p increase for hosted-api; initial correlation to model-serving nodes with high cache miss rates
2026-02-14T03:20Z - Oncall diagnosed disproportionate eviction churn on nodes serving multiple top-tier tenants
2026-02-14T03:32Z - Emergency mitigation: enabled eviction_throttle config to 0.5 and rolled a temporary kernel-scheduler revert (runtime commit e8a3d7)
2026-02-14T04:05Z - Traffic routing: shifted 30% of traffic from affected AZ to warm standby region, observed recovery of 95p latency within 12 minutes
2026-02-14T05:00Z - Post-incident triage started; heap snapshots taken and compaction logs collected
2026-02-15 - Root-cause draft: eviction score decay function allowed negative transient scores during concurrent reweighting; compaction preemption exposed refcount lifetime bug
root_cause: A previously merged optimization to accelerate eviction score recalculation (PR 12984) introduced a race where concurrent per-tenant reweighting could temporarily invert global eviction priorities. This was compounded by compaction preemption where slab entries' reference counts were decremented off the main write path, and a rare interleaving left references unreleased until a full GC/compaction cycle, appearing as memory leak under sustained churn.
mitigations_applied: Reverted PR 12984 in runtime (rolled back on 2026-02-14, release runtime-2.4.0-hotfix)
Enabled eviction_throttle and conservative smoothing window (config: eviction.smoothing_ms=3000) to reduce churn while patch is validated
Manual compaction run and forced slab GC on affected nodes; increased logging for refcount deltas
Traffic shifting and autoscaler guard (capped scale-to-zero for warm pools) to avoid thrash during recovery
decisions: Do not reintroduce score recalculation optimization until deterministic single-threaded validation is complete
Introduce a configuration gate for aggressive eviction heuristics; default off for multi-tenant fleets
Treat the slab refcount release path as safety-critical: require unit tests and a concurrency fuzz harness before merging fixes
Add target telemetry and SLO alerts for cross-tenant eviction imbalance (new metric: kvcache.eviction.cross_tenant_ratio)

rollout_plan: Deploy fixes to canary subset (5% of runtime shards) and run targeted traffic profile for 24h
If metrics stable, expand to 25% after 24h, then 60% after 48h; full rollout after 72h
Feature gate for aggressive eviction heuristics will be disabled by default; opt-in per-tenant via config flag
Monitor kvcache.hit_rate, kvcache.evictions_per_min, kvcache.cross_tenant_ratio, memory_resident_bytes during rollout
verification_criteria: No >15% drop in 95p cache hit rate for top-200 tenants for 72h post-rollout
Eviction churn reduced by >=70% compared to pre-fix baseline during peak traffic window
No sustained increase in resident memory >5% across nodes beyond normal seasonality
Observed reduction in autoscaler thrash events during controlled load tests
